text:
jeff: heads-up: aps2b cluster showing intermittent GPU segfaults on node-aps2b-17 + burst of correctable ECCs. auto-drain kicked for that host. seeing 15-22% increase in queue latency for dedicated pools in region. :rotating_light:

anya: can you paste the node logs and the drain command you ran?

jeff: logs attached to ops -> node-aps2b-17 (link) but snippet: 
```
kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
nvidia: GPU 0: correctable ECC errors rising (count 112 -> 240 in 30m)
oom-kill: python3  pid=2345 oom_reaper
```

jeff: ran: `redwoodctl node drain node-aps2b-17 --reason "hw-ecc/spike" --grace 300` then `redwoodctl node cordon node-aps2b-17`

sre-bot: ALERT aps2b-gpu-err-rate HIGH -- nodes affected: 1/96 -- impacted pools: dedicated-eu-west-2, burstpool-aps2b -- auto-drain active. ticket #INC-4673 created.

mohammed: ok, next steps: 1) keep node cordoned, 2) reprobe DIMMs and nvlink, 3) escalate to hw-rma if board-level faults. Can someone run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `dmesg | tail -n 200` and paste?

anya: pasted `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` to ops with output showing rising single-bit counts on GPU0 and GPU2. dmesg shows repeated Xid 79.

lina: rolling spare rotation plan: move 10% of dedicated traffic to aps3a for next 2h, enable cheaper quantized variants for low-latency tiers to reduce burst cost. I'll run traffic-shift and update routing policy.

jeff: noted. we need to minimize SLA impact for Dedicated customers — can we use canary route rules so only non-committed capacity goes to aps3a?

lina: yes — doing a staged reroute:
```
redwoodctl route update --pool dedicated-eu-west-2 --fallback aps3a:0.2 --canary 5m
```

mohammed: also suggest temporarily disabling large batch windows for that pool (reduce batch.size from 32 -> 8) to avoid long tail latency while capacity is constrained. that buys headroom.

jeff: agree. lina, can you also toggle batching?

lina: on it: `redwoodctl pool config set dedicated-eu-west-2 batching.max_tokens=1024 batching.max_requests=8`

deploy-bot: Deploys: routing-change v2 started by lina — CI passed — rolling 3/3 nodes. ETA 4m.

anya: operational note: this will increase per-token cost ~18% while bursted. raising finance FYI.

mohammed: hardware path: looks like memory controller on PCIe riser is flaky; we should schedule board-swap for node-aps2b-17. Lina, can you block the host for RMA and request spare board from stock?

lina: filing RMA request now. Estimated transit and replacement: 48-72h if local stock insufficient. I put a priority request for same-day courier.

jeff: if RMA is delayed >24h we should reprovision with a hot-spare GPU in aps2b to keep pool capacity. who owns spares inventory?

mohammed: inventory team is ops-hardware. tagging them in ticket. If no spare, we can reimage another low-usage host and move a GPU there, but that'll take ~90m.

anya: monitoring: setting up regression alerts for dedicated latency and error-rate. also adding probe to track correctable->uncorrectable threshold crossing.

sre-bot: MONITOR UPDATE: dedicated-eu-west-2 latency SLO breach probability 6% -> mitigations applied (routing shift + batching tweak). Continuing to watch.

jeff: communications: I'll prepare short note for customers on Dedicated status (emphasize mitigation steps + ETA). Lina loop me in on wording.

lina: drafting now, will post to status.redwood and ping account reps for impacted customers.

mohammed: postmortem checklist for after: collect ECC counts, nvlink logs, kernel dump, RMA serials, time-to-failure, and confirm whether quantization/fallback routing masked any correctness regressions.

jeff: thanks all. next update in 20m or on new material. :thumbsup:
